notes.title: No more fake tool calls
items: Some models, especially uncensored ones, sometimes typed out a tool call as text instead of actually running it, so the task just ended there. VORTEX now spots those and runs them for real, and the messy tags no longer show in the chat.

notes.title: Smooth updates
items: Fixed an error box (“resource busy or locked”) that could pop up while updating. A second download can no longer start once the update is already installing.
Old update files are cleaned up by themselves.
Quotes and dashes in the update log show properly instead of strange symbols.

notes.title: Commands that never hang
items: Commands can no longer get stuck for half an hour. A command that keeps going is stopped after 90 seconds (the AI can ask for up to 15 minutes when a build really needs it), and everything it started is closed too.
Programs that ask you to type something no longer wait forever. They get an empty answer at once and the AI carries on.
Loaders, servers and apps that are meant to keep running now start in the background: the AI sees their first few seconds of output and moves on while they keep running.
The live steps show the actual command, like “Running npm run build”, instead of just “Running a command”.

notes.title: Many chats at once
items: Chats now run side by side. Start a big task in one chat, open another chat and keep talking there. The first one keeps working in the background, and nothing needs to be stopped.
Chats that are still working show a small spinning logo in the chat list, so you can see which ones are busy.
Go back to a busy chat any time and you see it working live, right where it is.
On Android, the camera now fills the whole screen like a normal camera app, with a big shutter button, your photos along the bottom, and a Done button.

notes.title: Finishes what it starts
items: Big tasks no longer stop halfway. VORTEX can now keep working for up to 150 steps in a row, instead of stopping after 12.
If the connection drops for a moment in the middle of a task, VORTEX picks up where it left off instead of quitting.
If the AI stops early with steps still left on its checklist, VORTEX reminds it to carry on and finish them.
Long answers that hit the length limit carry straight on.
Every finished reply now says how long it took, like “Done in 25m” or “Done in 8s”.
On the phone, long tasks no longer look stopped: it stays connected to your PC the whole time, and reconnects by itself if the signal drops.

notes.title: You can see it working
items: The checkpoint list stays on screen the whole time while VORTEX works with tools, and ticks off each step. It no longer disappears halfway.
No more walls of write_file rows. All the tools a reply used fold into one line, “Used 9 tools”, in plain words like “Wrote notes.txt” or “Ran a command”. Tap it to see each one.
A live line under the reply always shows what is happening right now, like “Writing run.ps1…” or “Thinking about the next step…”, so it never looks stopped.
Long tool runs keep the live steps short: the newest few, plus a count of the ones already done.

notes.title: Remote with just a sign-in
items: No more links. On your phone, tap “Sign in with my PC account”, type the username and password you use on your PC, and the phone runs on your PC.
If your PC restarts Remote, the phone finds it again by itself.
Remote stays on after you restart your PC, so the phone can always find it while VORTEX AI is open.
Your PC's address is locked with your password, so only you can find your PC.

notes.title: Sign in your way
items: The phone has its own sign-in again. Linking it to your PC no longer signs you in by itself.
Signing out on the phone only signs out the phone, not your PC.
Sign out is now also in Settings → Account.
Updates on the PC work even when the Vortex server is down: the app picks up the newest version straight from this PC.

notes.title: Updates arrive again
items: The update log and the download button work on the phone again: while the phone is connected to your PC, updates are served from the PC instead of the old server that is offline.
Late 1.9.0 fixes rolled in: the phone no longer shows the setup card while it is attached to a PC.

notes.title: Phone does what the PC does
items: On Android, paste the Remote link from your PC (or tap "Or use your PC" on the first screen) and the phone runs on your PC: the same account, the same chats and every model, with no sign-in and no key on the phone.
The phone keeps the link; if the PC is asleep it says so instead of looking broken.
Bigger header, larger bottom tabs and roomier settings rows on phones so it is not cramped.
The PC shows a chat called "From your phone" and the phone sees your normal chat list.

notes.title: Remote, one click, and a whip
items: Remote: turn it on in Settings → Remote and open the link on your phone. The phone gets the same models and the same PC tools while you are away, and the PC just has to stay on. Each link is private and dies when you switch Remote off.
Tools run on their own now. No approval pop-ups; switch any single tool back to Ask in MCP & tools.
Roblox Studio connects with one click. Nothing to type, no command or transport.
Live steps only show for real work now. A hello gets a plain answer.
Whip, in Tools: grab the lash, swing it, crack the tip. Every crack makes it faster.

notes.title: Whole PC and the web
items: The AI can reach your whole PC now. Relative paths start at your folder, and absolute paths reach any drive. Read, search, write and run commands anywhere.
It can use the web too: open a page or API, search, and download a file straight to disk.
Writes, downloads and commands always ask first, with the exact path shown.
The Files tab stays in the side panel, and Roblox Studio no longer loads itself into every chat. Switch it on under MCP & tools when you want it.

notes.title: The new Vortex AI
items: Brand-new look: clean graphite design, a new spiral logo and app icon, and an icon rail on the left.
Vortex 1, our own model: it picks the best model for every message (code, maths, writing, photos) and switches if one is busy. 100 credits a day, unlimited for the Owner.
Memory: Vortex remembers your name, your style and your projects, uses them in later chats, and shows every save with Undo. Edit it all in Settings → Memory.
Checkpoints: big tasks show a live plan with each step ticking off. Tap a step to jump to it.
Home has Ask, Study and Build modes, and a moving code background that ripples when you tap it.
Type your next message while Vortex is still answering. It sends by itself when the answer finishes.
Ctrl F finds words in a chat, and typing / gives quick commands like /remember, /quiz and /flashcards.
Updates now install from inside the app.
Create an account from the sign-in screen; the first account on a PC is still the Owner.
You stay signed in after closing the app; Sign out still clears it.

notes.title: Tools and live steps
items: Notes, a focus timer and Math Sprint in the Tools panel.
Live steps show what the AI is doing while it answers.
Uncensored models for the Owner, and a usage meter in the chat box.

notes.title: Redesign, part one
items: New home screen with a greeting, the ask box, quick actions and recent chats.
Command palette with Ctrl K, and a full-screen model picker with Ctrl M.
Study tools: flashcards and quizzes made from any topic.
Phone layout: top bar, drawer and bottom tabs.
Answer actions: read aloud, or retry with another model.
Free Experiential models are usable at a zero balance.

notes.title: Study tools
items: Flashcards and quizzes made from any topic.
Read answers aloud, and retry an answer with another model.

notes.title: Homework mode
items: Homework button with Casual, Clear and Polished writing levels, correct answers and numbered steps with reasons.
Maths rendered properly, and simple diagrams when they help.
Photos from the picker, camera, paste or drag-and-drop.
Models without vision get the text read off the photo by offline OCR, and a notice saying so.
